title: Jesus prays (CCC 2598–2606)
hookLine: he prays at every big moment of his life

cards: Before a big choice, out comes the list. Pros, cons. A call to a friend, a night to sleep on it, other people's opinions scrolled at midnight.
Luke's Gospel tells about the night before Jesus chose the twelve apostles, the men who would carry on his work. He didn't make a list.
He went up a mountain to pray, and in the Douay-Rheims, "he passed the whole night in the prayer of God." When day came, he chose twelve.

teach.h: LUKE: PRAYER AT THE TURNING POINTS.
teach.b: Luke's Gospel, the Catechism points out, keeps showing Jesus praying at the turning points. At his baptism in the Jordan, while he prays, the heavens open. Before choosing the Twelve, a whole night.

Before Peter says who Jesus is, he has been praying alone. On the mountain of the Transfiguration, his face changes as he prays. And a quieter habit: he often slipped away to lonely places, sometimes at night, to pray.
As a boy, the Catechism says, Jesus learned to pray with his human heart from his mother, and in the synagogue and the Temple, with the words and rhythms of his people.
Yet his prayer comes from somewhere deeper: his relationship with the Father. Listen to how his prayers begin.
At the tomb of Lazarus, before he calls his friend out, he says, "Father, I give thee thanks that thou hast heard me."
Then the garden, the night before he dies, in Luke: "not my will, but thine be done." The garden, the Catechism says, gives a glimpse of the depth of his prayer as Son: trust, and a will handed over.
Mark keeps the Aramaic word he used: Abba, Father. Even on the cross he prays, for the ones crucifying him, and at the end he commends his spirit into his Father's hands.
In the Catechism's picture, Jesus isn't only the one Christians pray to. He prayed first, and taught by doing it.

how: Catholics look to Jesus as the model of prayer, and some keep his habits: prayer before decisions, time alone in quiet, thanksgiving, and the garden's handing over of the will, echoed in the Lord's Prayer's thy will be done.

games.q: tomorrow you'll choose the twelve who will carry on your work. what do you do tonight?
o: ask the crowd who they'd pick.
pick the ones who've followed longest.
games.why: Luke says he went up a mountain and passed the whole night in prayer. when day came, he chose the Twelve.

practice: Bring to mind one choice in front of you, large or small, and don't weigh it or make the list yet; just hold it, the way Jesus took the night before choosing.
If you pray, bring it to God, and if you're ready, add the words from the garden. If you don't, let it rest in quiet before you decide.

wordCard.voice: Jesus prays. In the Gospels, at his baptism, before choosing the Twelve, on the mountain, in the garden and on the cross: in Catholic teaching, the one who prays first, and teaches by praying. Today's word.
